newsitem.title: MEXICO: La Moderna says close to deal on Royal Van Namen.
newsitem.headline: La Moderna says close to deal on Royal Van Namen.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Empresas La Moderna is close to a deal to buy Dutch fresh produce distributor Royal Van Namen, company officials said.
"With regards to Royal Van Namen, I expect that within a month, month-and-a-half, we will have closed the deal," Alfonso Romo, the CEO of La Moderna, told Reuters in an interview.
With annual sales of some $50 million, Van Namen is one of Europe's largest produce distributors and would add to La Moderna's growing network of distribution in the Americas.
Romo said produce would be shipped to Europe from the Americas and vice-versa.
La Moderna grows and buys fresh produce from Chile to Canada. About 75 percent of its production is currently sold in the United States and Canada.

"The fragmented fresh produce market with the largest player capturing only 7 percent of the market is fertile ground for (La Moderna) to leverage its vast distribution capabilities," Terry Sigler, an analyst at Flemings Research brokerage in New York, said in a recent report.
Sigler said demand in the U.S. fresh produce market is expected to grow more than 10 percent a year. He has a long-term buy rating on La Moderna.

A pure cigarette company just three years ago, La Moderna has expanded into agrobiotechnology and packaging. Its agrobiotechnology division consists of a fresh produce division and a seeds company Seminis.
"We used our infrastructure for tobacco, which we used just five months a year, to expand into other crops ... We want to produce vegetables 12 months a year for export," Romo said.
Romo said its produce division exported $250 million worth of vegetables last year. Moderna's produce company Bionova just merged with Oakland-based DNA Plant Technology to form DNAP Holdings.
